test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 23 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In February 2024, who was sworn in as the first woman Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ritu Bahri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Justice **Ritu Bahri** was sworn in as the first woman Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court in **February 2024**.
 
• She is a distinguished judge who previously served at the **Punjab and Haryana High Court**.
 
• Justice Ritu Bahri brings decades of judicial experience and expertise to her new role as Chief Justice.
 
• The appointment of Justice Bahri marks a significant milestone in gender representation within the Indian judiciary.
 
• Her elevation is in line with efforts to ensure greater diversity and inclusivity in higher judicial positions in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uttarakhand High Court:**

 
 
• Established in **2000**, following the creation of the state of Uttarakhand.
 
• Located in **Nainital**, it handles cases pertaining to the state and exercises jurisdiction over civil, criminal, and constitutional matters.
 
 
 
• **Women in Indian Judiciary:**
 
 
• Justice **Fathima Beevi** was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India, appointed in 1989.
 
• Efforts are being made to increase the representation of women in higher judicial positions, including appointments of women Chief Justices.
 
 
 
• **Role of a Chief Justice:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of a High Court is responsible for the administrative and judicial functioning of the court.
 
• They ensure fair hearings, timely disposal of cases, and adherence to constitutional values.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Appointments in India:**
 
 
• High Court judges are appointed by the President of India after consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the respective state.
 
• The process emphasizes merit, seniority, and integrity.
